description: Sabotages for windows-file-enumeration-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are. Begun with PATH-1, so it covers the path contract this crate now takes from windows-namespace-request-sys and nothing older.
notCoveredHere: The graft's own rules are the request crate's and are sabotaged in its manifest (the NR-3.3 entries); this one covers only this crate's use of them. A failure to read the current directory cannot be made by a test, so the code it carries is a declared survivor.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the worker opens the path as given and not the grafted one
sabotages.why: The two name the same directory until the current directory moves, so only the child-process test that moves it after the request is built tells them apart.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the path as given is reported as the grafted one
sabotages.why: path() is documented as the path the caller gave, and a relative one differs from what the worker opens.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: an interior NUL is reported as a failure to read the current directory
sabotages.why: The two failures say different things to the caller, and only the first is about the path itself.

sabotages.name: PATH-1: the code of a failure to read the current directory is dropped
sabotages.why: Declared, and not a gap a test can close: GetCurrentDirectoryW cannot be made to fail from a test without breaking the process it runs in. What would reach it is a fault seam in the request crate's current-directory read, which it does not have.

sabotages.name: PATH-1 control: the request's path is built through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same value through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
